key_insight: Combining persona and knowledge directions can improve lie ranking over same-depth supervised probes, but transfer varies by model and deception type.
engineering_relevance: Label-free activation directions offer a low-cost approach to deception monitoring, but require model-specific validation and controls for wording effects.
method: Expand an honest/deceptive persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they possess.
Extract middle-layer persona directions and knowledge directions using identical scripted denials for answerable and unanswerable questions.
Evaluate individual and summed directions against supervised probes and random-direction baselines.
evidence_signal: Across four models on Liars’ Bench, persona directions outperform single-dataset probes on three, while summed directions outperform same-depth supervised probes on all four, with one comparison near chance.
watch_item: Persona directions largely track wording on knowledge-denial tasks; gains are inconsistent, and the combined direction trails the supervised probe on held-out lies.
paper_title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
